reference.title: Cable Reverse Preacher Curl
reference.listing: Video (title and number from the catalog listing; the page could not be read from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, a short squeeze, about 2.4 s down

prescription.tempo: 1 s up, brief squeeze, 2-3 s down
prescription.progression: Add load in small steps; slower lowering

cues.text: Sit at the preacher bench facing a low pulley, upper arms flat on the pad; overhand grip on the straight bar about shoulder width.
Breathe out and curl the bar up with the palms down, elbows on the pad, wrists straight.
Squeeze with the forearms about vertical.
Breathe in and lower slowly until the arm is nearly straight; keep the elbow on the pad.
Stop just short of locking out; repeat.

mistakes.fix: Keep the knuckles in line with the forearms.

mistakes.mistake: Lifting the elbows off the pad
mistakes.fix: Keep the upper arms on the pad.
Use about half your underhand load.

kinematics.norm: Full range from nearly straight arms to about 120-130 degrees; mean elbow range was about 117-123 degrees across standing barbell, EZ-bar and dumbbell curls (Marcolin 2018)

kinematics.measure: Forearm rotation (wrist pron channel, 0 = palm up/forward, 90 = thumb up)
kinematics.norm: Pronated grip: brachioradialis activity rises and biceps activity falls compared with a supinated grip (Coratella 2023)

kinematics.measure: Upper arm from the trunk line (sagittal)
kinematics.norm: Shoulder flexed with the upper arm on the pad: preacher curls load the elbow flexors at short muscle lengths compared with shoulder-extended curls (Attarieh 2025)

kinematics.measure: Upper arm on the pad (rig shapes)
kinematics.norm: Upper arm and elbow stay on the pad throughout (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1 s up and 2-3 s down (clinical opinion); biceps activity was lower while lowering than lifting at the same load (Oliveira 2009)

Oliveira, Matta, Alves, Garcia and Vieira 2009, effect of the shoulder position on the biceps brachii EMG in different dumbbell curls (J Sports Sci Med 8(1):24-29)

cautions: Elbow: the bottom of a preacher curl stretches the biceps and the front of the elbow under load; lower slowly and stop short of locking out (clinical opinion).
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Lighter load and a shorter range at the bottom.
regressions: Shorter range: stop the lowering at about 30 degrees of elbow bend.

muscleNotes.forearm_extensors: Brachioradialis and the wrist extensors work hard with the palms down (Coratella 2023).
muscleNotes.biceps: Biceps still flex the elbow but less than with an underhand grip (Coratella 2023).

phases.label: Arm nearly straight on the pad
